answer: Stop sybils with an orchard onyx pigment: an agent stakes a bond for one orchard row. Each cycle it grafts a shoot and ties an onyx tag with a pigment stripe; verifiers match its hue to the row soil chart, voiding a row whose tag is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 rows at 18x: each tag fits one orchard and one pigment, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents graft once, keep rights.
